title: Omelette aux Fines Herbes
subtitle: French herb omelette
excerpt: A French rolled omelette made with chervil, chives, parsley, and tarragon. The eggs stay pale and soft inside, with a barely coloured exterior. It takes under two minutes once the pan is hot.

recipe.sourceNotes: The French rolled omelette is one of the fundamental dishes of the French kitchen. Fines herbes (chervil, chives, parsley, and tarragon) is a classic combination described by Escoffier and many French cookery writers as the standard herb mixture for omelettes and sauces.

recipeTools.notes: A non-stick pan no more than 24 cm across so the egg is deep enough to roll.

content.text: Omelette aux fines herbes is a classic French rolled omelette made with the four herbs: chervil, chives, parsley, and tarragon. The egg stays pale yellow and creamy inside, barely set, with a smooth exterior that is not allowed to brown. Getting there is about a very hot pan, quick movement, and confidence.

Break the eggs into a bowl. Add the salt, pepper, and most of the herbs, keeping a pinch back for finishing. Beat with a fork for about 15 seconds until the whites and yolks are just combined, with a little streakiness still visible.
Heat a 22 to 24 cm non-stick frying pan over a high heat until it is very hot. Add the butter. When the butter stops foaming and is just beginning to turn pale gold, pour in the egg mixture.

Immediately begin to move the egg with the flat of a fork, pulling the set edges into the centre while tilting the pan to let liquid egg flow out to the sides. Stop stirring when the egg is mostly set but still looks wet on the surface, about 45 seconds.

Tilt the pan handle end up. Use the fork to fold the near edge of the omelette towards the centre. Then tip the omelette onto a warm plate by rolling it out of the pan, folded side down, so it lands seam-side down with a curved shape.
Scatter the reserved herbs over the top and serve immediately.
